findings.claim: _current_signing_key_id raises ValueError with an identical 'not configured — provision a key ring' message across all three failure modes, including the case where the key ring file IS present but contains no line marked current=true. The message prescribes wrong remediation for the active-key-absent scenario.
findings.evidence: tools.py:679-682 (file absent): raise ValueError('signing key ring not configured at docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub; cannot record signing_key_id - provision a key ring before using propose()'). tools.py:684-690 (OSError): identical message. tools.py:705-708 (loop exhausted, no current=true match): identical message. The 'provision a key ring' instruction is correct for the first two cases but wrong for the third — the key ring IS provisioned; the operator needs to add current=1/true/yes to an existing key line, not provision a new file. test_propose_rejects_when_no_current_signing_key_is_marked (line 227) asserts only 'cannot record signing_key_id' in response.message, which passes for all three paths and does not distinguish them.
findings.impact: An operator who configures a key ring with a valid ssh-ed25519 line but omits current=true receives 'provision a key ring' as remediation advice. Following this advice, they would either recreate the file (unnecessary) or rotate the key (potentially disruptive). The actual fix — adding current=true to the existing key line — is not suggested. Downstream diagnostic tooling that pattern-matches the error message cannot distinguish a missing-file failure from a misconfigured-key failure; both emit the same string, making automated triage incorrect.
findings.mitigation: Differentiate the third failure path at tools.py:705-708 with a distinct message: 'signing key ring at docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub exists but contains no key marked current=1, current=true, or current=yes; annotate the intended active key before using propose()'. Add a test asserting this distinct message substring for the no-active-key path, separate from the file-absent assertion in test_propose_requires_a_configured_signing_key_ring.

findings.claim: The while True slot-search loop in propose_impl (tools.py:1162-1174) has no iteration upper bound. With N orphaned proposals/PROP-NNN branches, the loop makes N sequential git show-ref calls (each up to DEFAULT_GIT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30s) while holding _PROPOSAL_LOCK, blocking all concurrent callers.
findings.evidence: tools.py:1161: next_proposal_number = int(_next_proposal_id(proposals_root).removeprefix('PROP-')). tools.py:1162-1174: while True — increments next_proposal_number whenever _proposal_branch_exists returns True; no guard of the form 'if next_proposal_number > some_limit: return _error(...)'. This is residual from R1 C-MIN-01, not targeted in fr1. The _remove_orphaned_duplicate_proposals call earlier in the same guard removes only orphaned files (no branch), not orphaned branches (no file). An environment with many orphaned branches — from repeated SIGKILL-after-branch-creation scenarios — still forces the full scan.
findings.impact: With 100 orphaned branches, lock hold time up to 3000s. All concurrent propose() callers queue behind _PROPOSAL_LOCK. Legitimate callers time out. The fr1 orphan-file recovery does not reduce the number of orphaned branches, so this path remains reachable under repeated process-kill incidents that succeed in creating the branch before dying.
findings.mitigation: Add an explicit iteration cap (e.g., 1024) before the while True body: if next_proposal_number > initial_number + 1024: return _error('SCP-MCP-E021', 'proposal ID space exhausted after 1024 attempts; remove orphaned proposals/PROP-NNN branches'). Also consider tightening the per-call timeout for _proposal_branch_exists inside this loop (5s is sufficient for a local ref lookup).

findings.claim: _stdio_caller_id() falls back to Path.cwd().resolve() when sys.argv is empty or sys.argv[0] is whitespace-only, producing caller_id = 'stdio:<pid>:<cwd>'. The U-21-f resolution column in plan §13 documents the derivation exclusively as 'stdio:<pid>:<resolved argv[0] path>' without mentioning the fallback.
findings.evidence: tools.py:672: executable_path = Path(sys.argv[0]).resolve() if sys.argv and sys.argv[0].strip() else Path.cwd().resolve(). WP-SCP-021 §13 U-21-f Resolution (line 250): 'caller_id is derived from the live stdio server process as stdio:<pid>:<resolved argv[0] path>'. CWD fallback absent from resolution text. Residual from R1 C-nit-01 and SB-MIN-006; not targeted in fr1.
findings.impact: In embedded Python contexts or test harnesses that clear sys.argv, the fallback fires silently. Two different server binaries in the same working directory with argv[0]='' share a caller_id prefix and merge their rate-limit quotas. The U-21-f resolution text records behaviour that diverges from the implementation, misleading future reviewers of 021I.
findings.mitigation: Replace the CWD fallback with sys.executable (always populated by CPython) or with a clearly labelled sentinel 'stdio:<pid>:unknown-executable' accompanied by a log.warning. Update the U-21-f Resolution column to document the actual fallback. Add a test that monkeypatches sys.argv to [] and asserts the caller_id contains a clearly labelled fallback token rather than a bare CWD path.

structured_review.summary: All six R1 MAJ findings verified closed in fr1. One new MIN found (R2-C-MIN-01). One MIN residual (R2-C-MIN-02). Two nit residuals. Slice meets §4.3 MAJ-threshold fixpoint criterion; fr2 needed before MIN gate closes.

verifications.evidence: _remove_orphaned_duplicate_proposals (tools.py:792-807) called at lines 1114-1126 before rate-limit and dedupe checks. Iterates existing proposals; for each whose proposal_hash matches AND whose branch does not exist, unlinks the file. test_propose_recovers_orphaned_duplicate_after_unclean_branch_creation_failure verifies re-submit succeeds after orphan.

_current_signing_key_id now raises ValueError in all three failure paths (tools.py:679-682 file absent, 684-690 OSError, 705-708 no current=true key). propose_impl catches ValueError at 1109-1112 and returns SCP-MCP-E021. test_propose_requires_a_configured_signing_key_ring and test_propose_rejects_when_no_current_signing_key_is_marked both assert SCP-MCP-E021.

Option A applied: mcp-error-codes.md §SCP-MCP-E020 now reads 'For stdio callers, the hourly limit is advisory because the caller key is pid + executable path; the branch-not-main invariant remains the hard safety boundary across process restarts.' Advisory caveat correctly scoped to stdio; code behavior unchanged by design.

Same fix as C-MAJ-02. All three signing-key failure paths raise ValueError; no sentinel written to proposal metadata. test_propose_records_envelope_fields_with_stdio_identity asserts signing_key_id equals 'scp-mcp-hardening-key' from a live key-ring read (signing_key_id param not passed to propose_impl, so _current_signing_key_id is exercised).

ProposeRequest.title has max_length=_PROPOSAL_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH (500) and body has max_length=_PROPOSAL_BODY_MAX_LENGTH (65536) at tools.py:199-200. _proposal_rate_limit_exceeded (lines 642-659) now breaks on first record with queued_at < cutoff or queued_at not a datetime (early-exit added). _iter_existing_proposals accepts max_records=_PROPOSAL_SCAN_LIMIT (2048) cap. test_propose_request_rejects_oversized_title_and_body and test_iter_existing_proposals_caps_scan_volume cover these paths.

tools.py:749 now emits '> proposals queue until adjudication ships. Status updates via' (word 'land' removed). test_propose_injects_the_silent_rot_banner_front_matter (test_propose_hardening.py:130-160) asserts the corrected string verbatim including branch name interpolation.
